A CNC machine combines a controller, motor drives, axes, home and limit switches, spindle or tool control, coordinate systems, work offsets, G-code, and motion planning.

| Layer | Role |
|:--|:--|
| CAD | defines geometry |
| CAM | selects tools and creates toolpaths |
| G-code | expresses motion and machine functions |
| controller | plans and coordinates motion |
| drives and motors | move axes and tool systems |
| machine process | creates the finished part |

Open-loop stepper systems assume commanded steps produced motion. Closed-loop servo systems measure motion and correct error. Both architectures need homing, limits, interlocks, and an emergency-stop strategy suitable for the machine.

LinuxCNC provides G-code interpretation, real-time motion control, hardware connections through HAL, and support for open-loop stepper or closed-loop servo systems. Review the official [LinuxCNC architecture](https://linuxcnc.org/docs/master/html/en/getting-started/about-linuxcnc.html).
